references.text: God's command to Abraham that all in his household shall be circumcised - both those born in the house and those bought with money from a foreigner. Verse 27 is the direct fulfillment of this command.
Abraham circumcises Ishmael and all the men in his household, both those born in the house and those bought with money, on the same day God spoke to him.
Abraham had 318 home-born (יְלִידֵי) servants, which provides context for the scope of those 'born in the house' who were circumcised.
All the men of Shechem's city were circumcised, a parallel to how all the men in Abraham's household were circumcised - circumcision imposed on an entire group.
Any servant bought with money must be circumcised before he may eat of the Passover lamb - a parallel to the circumcision of those bought with money in Abraham's household.
A foreigner who wishes to celebrate Passover must have all the men in his household circumcised, extending the principle that the entire household shall be circumcised.
17:13 is the very command for circumcision of the men of the house, while 17:27 is the actual fulfillment of this command.
17:12 defines the criteria for who must be circumcised, which explains the extensive list of persons in 17:27.
Both verses illustrate a moment when an entire group of men chooses circumcision, highlighting the ritual's role as a marker of identity.
18:19 gives the theological basis for Abraham's action in 17:27: to lead his household to righteousness.
Paul in Rom 4:16 expands the concept of 'Abraham's household' from the physical circumcision in 17:27 to a spiritual family based on faith.
